mcqs.q: Compared with stainless steel, carbon steel instruments are:
opts: Harder and keep a keen edge, but corrode (rust) if unprotected
mcqs.explain: Carbon steel is harder and retains a keen cutting edge longer, but it corrodes/rusts; stainless steel stays bright but loses its edge faster.

mcqs.q: Marzouk's classification of hand instruments includes:
mcqs.explain: Marzouk classified hand instruments as diagnostic, cutting, restoring and finishing/polishing instruments.

mcqs.q: Which is a use of the mouth mirror?
opts: Indirect vision, light reflection and soft-tissue retraction
mcqs.explain: The mouth mirror gives indirect vision (esp. upper teeth), reflects light and retracts soft tissues (tongue, cheek, lip).

mcqs.q: The pointed tip of an explorer is called the:
mcqs.explain: An explorer is a delicate pointed instrument for tactile examination; its tip is called the tine.

mcqs.q: In operative dentistry, the periodontal probe is useful to:
opts: Measure the dimensions of cavity preparations
mcqs.explain: Besides measuring pocket depth, in operative dentistry the periodontal probe is used to measure cavity-preparation dimensions.

mcqs.q: Cotton pliers (tweezers) are used to:
opts: Place/remove cotton rolls and carry pellets or wedges
mcqs.explain: Cotton pliers have angled tips for placing/removing cotton rolls and carrying small items (pellets, wedges).

mcqs.q: The three parts of a hand instrument are:
mcqs.explain: A hand instrument has a handle, a shank and a working end (blade or nib).

mcqs.q: The working end of a CUTTING instrument is a ___, while that of a RESTORING instrument is a ___:
mcqs.explain: The working end is a blade/cutting edge on cutting instruments and a nib on non-cutting (restoring) instruments.

mcqs.q: Contra-angling of the shank is designed to:
opts: Bring the cutting edge within 3 mm of the handle axis (anti-rotational balance)
mcqs.explain: Contra-angling angles the shank so the cutting edge lies within 3 mm of the handle's long axis, giving optimal anti-rotational balance.

mcqs.q: A single-beveled cutting instrument is the:
mcqs.explain: By bevel: single-beveled = chisel; bi-beveled = hatchet excavator; circumferentially beveled = spoon excavator.

mcqs.q: A circumferentially beveled instrument is the:
mcqs.explain: The spoon excavator has a spoon-shaped, circumferentially beveled blade; it is double-ended and removes soft caries.

mcqs.q: The straight chisel is primarily used to:
mcqs.explain: A chisel (straight or, if curved, Wedelstadt) is used mainly for removing unsupported enamel.

mcqs.q: The enamel hatchet is used to:
opts: Remove unsupported enamel from the proximal area in a Class II preparation
mcqs.explain: The enamel hatchet (single-beveled, straight blade, cutting edge parallel to the handle) removes unsupported proximal enamel in Class II preparations.

mcqs.q: The gingival marginal trimmer (GMT) differs from the enamel hatchet in that its blade is:
opts: Curved, with the cutting edge at an angle other than 90° (comes in mesial & distal pairs)
mcqs.explain: The GMT is like a hatchet but has a curved blade with the cutting edge at an angle; it comes in mesial and distal pairs.

mcqs.q: A primary use of the gingival marginal trimmer is:
opts: Bevelling the gingival wall and rounding the axiopulpal line angle in Class II
mcqs.explain: The GMT bevels the gingival wall and rounds/bevels the axiopulpal line angle in Class II preparations.

mcqs.q: The spoon excavator is mainly used to:
mcqs.explain: The spoon excavator removes soft carious dentin from the preparation.

mcqs.q: Which group does the mouth mirror belong to?
mcqs.explain: Mouth mirrors, explorers, periodontal probes and tweezers are diagnostic (exploring) instruments.

mcqs.q: Amalgam carriers, condensers, burnishers and carvers are classed as:
mcqs.explain: Restoring instruments include cement spatulas, plastic filling instruments, amalgam carriers, condensers, burnishers and carvers.

mcqs.q: An instrument with a shank, blade and cutting edge on BOTH ends of the handle is termed:
mcqs.explain: Instruments with working ends on both sides of the handle are double-ended (most hand instruments).

mcqs.q: Finishing strips, finishing burs, brushes and rubber cups are used for:
mcqs.explain: These belong to the finishing-and-polishing group used to finish and polish restorations.

mcqs.q: A monoangled shank has:
mcqs.explain: Shanks are straight (no angle), monoangled (one), binangled (two) or triple-angled (three).

mcqs.q: The disadvantage of carbon-steel instruments is that they:
mcqs.explain: Carbon steel, though hard and edge-retentive, corrodes/rusts when unprotected — a disadvantage compared with stainless steel.

saqs.q: Compare stainless and carbon steel for hand instruments.
saqs.a: Stainless: stays bright but loses its edge quickly. Carbon steel: harder, keeps a keen edge, but rusts.

saqs.q: List Marzouk's four classes of hand instruments.
Name the diagnostic instruments and a use of the mirror.
saqs.a: Mouth mirror, explorer, periodontal probe, tweezers. Mirror = indirect vision, light reflection, retraction.

saqs.q: Name the three parts of a hand instrument.
Classify cutting instruments by their bevels with an example.
saqs.a: Single-beveled = chisel; bi-beveled = hatchet excavator; circumferentially beveled = spoon excavator.

saqs.q: Give the use of the enamel hatchet and the gingival marginal trimmer.
saqs.a: Enamel hatchet: remove unsupported proximal enamel (Class II). GMT: bevel the gingival wall / round the axiopulpal line angle.

saqs.q: What is contra-angling and its purpose?
saqs.a: Angling the shank so the cutting edge is within 3 mm of the handle axis, giving optimal anti-rotational balance.
